body_markdown:
> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Campus network architecture

The campus network is a collapsed core: two **core switches** in the Network Room (MDF) of the Hub Building,
redundant **firewalls** and **WAN routers** towards two internet providers, and access switches in each building.

| Layer | Equipment | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Edge | [WAN router 01](/assets/nf-rtr-wan-01), [WAN router 02](/assets/nf-rtr-wan-02) | Hub, MDF, rack R-MDF1 |
| Security | [Firewall 01](/assets/nf-fw-01) (active), [Firewall 02](/assets/nf-fw-02) (standby) | Hub, MDF |
| Core | [Core switch 01](/assets/nf-sw-core-01), [Core switch 02](/assets/nf-sw-core-02) | Hub, MDF |
| Distribution | [Data hall distribution switch](/assets/nf-sw-dist-dh) | Hub, Data Hall A, R-A01 |
| Access | [Library access switch](/assets/nf-sw-acc-lib), [Annex access switch](/assets/nf-sw-acc-anx) | over single-mode fibre |

## VLANs

Servers (10), staff (20), Wi-Fi staff (30), Wi-Fi guest (31), management (40), storage and backup (50).

## Resilience

Each core switch takes one UPS feed (A from [UPS-01](/assets/nf-ups-01), B from [UPS-02](/assets/nf-ups-02)).
A failure of one core switch is handled by the [failover runbook](/documents/nf-doc-failover).

See the diagram attached to this revision.

> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Change Advisory Board — 21 October 2026

Present: Mara Ellison (chair), Teo Lindqvist, Priya Nandakumar, Sam Okafor.

1. **Core switch firmware 10.4 → 10.6** (NF-T-003): approved for Saturday 7 November, 06:00–09:00.
2. **UPS-02 battery replacement** (NF-T-007): approved, 14 November, no outage expected (UPS on bypass).
3. **Guest Wi-Fi for the conference** (NF-T-008): standard change, no board needed.

> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Change management

Every change to a production service is a **Change** ticket: what, why, the risk, the rollback, the window.

* Standard changes (listed in the service catalogue) need no board.
* Normal changes are reviewed by the Change Advisory Board on Tuesdays.
* Emergency changes are approved by the duty manager and reviewed at the next board.

Maintenance windows: Saturday 06:00–09:00 for network and storage, Sunday 07:00–10:00 for hosting.

> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Service desk handbook

How the [Service Desk](/assets/nf-svc-desk) takes, sorts and follows requests:

* **Incident** — something stopped working: restore first, investigate after.
* **Service request** — something new from the catalogue: a VLAN, an account, guest access.
* **Problem** — the cause behind repeated incidents.
* **Change** — any change to production, through the Change Advisory Board.

Priorities follow the service's tier and how many people are affected.

> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Data Hall A — rack layout and power budget

Six racks (R-A01 to R-A06) in one cold aisle, two close-control units (CRAC-01, CRAC-02), A and B feeds from UPS-01
and UPS-02. Budget: 6 kW a rack, 30 kW cooling each CRAC (N+1).

| Rack | Holds | Load (kW) |
|---|---|---|
| R-A01 | distribution switch, patch | 1.2 |
| R-A02 | hypervisor hosts 01, 02 | 4.8 |
| R-A03 | hypervisor hosts 03, 04 | 4.8 |
| R-A04 | STOR-01, NAS-01 | 3.9 |
| R-A05 | GPU-01, GPU-02 (batch), fabric switch, model store, rear-door cooler | 11.2 |
| R-A06 | GPU-03, GPU-04 (inference), login node, scratch storage, rear-door cooler | 11.6 |

R-A05 and R-A06 are above the 6 kW air-cooled budget: each has a 15 kW rear-door cooler on the chilled water
(change NF-T-015).

The floor plan of the Hub Building's ground floor shows the racks where they stand.

> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Core switch failover

When [Core switch 01](/assets/nf-sw-core-01) or [Core switch 02](/assets/nf-sw-core-02) fails or is upgraded:

1. Check in [Monitoring](/assets/nf-svc-monitoring) that the peer switch carries all uplinks.
2. Shut the failed switch's uplinks to the distribution and access switches.
3. Confirm DHCP and DNS answers from both [NS-01](/assets/nf-vm-dns1) and [NS-02](/assets/nf-vm-dns2).
4. Replace or upgrade the switch; bring uplinks back one at a time.
5. Close with a note in the change ticket.

> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# HPC and LLM services — architecture

Four GPU servers in racks R-A05 and R-A06 share a 200 Gb/s fabric ([SW-FABRIC](/assets/nf-sw-fabric)) with the
[login node](/assets/nf-hpc-login) and the [parallel scratch storage](/assets/nf-stor-scratch).

* **HPC Batch Computing** — GPU-01 and GPU-02 form the *batch* partition of the scheduler
  ([SCHED-01](/assets/nf-vm-sched), Batchwell Scheduler). Users log in on LOGIN-01 and submit jobs.
* **LLM Inference** — GPU-03 and GPU-04 form the *inference* partition, serving the Fieldstone-13B model (a
  fictional open-weights model) with Inferna Serve. Requests reach them through the [LLM gateway](/assets/nf-vm-llmgw)
  (quotas, logging), which the AI assistant and the API use. Model weights are on [MODELS-01](/assets/nf-stor-models).

Both live on VLAN 60 (HPC and AI); the fabric carries only job and storage traffic. Power and cooling: the racks
are above the air-cooled budget and have rear-door coolers (see the Data Hall layout).

> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Restart the LLM inference service

1. In [Monitoring](/assets/nf-svc-monitoring), check which inference node is unhealthy (GPU-03 or GPU-04).
2. Drain it in the scheduler's *inference* partition; the [gateway](/assets/nf-vm-llmgw) sends requests to the other.
3. Restart the serving engine on that node; wait for the model to load from MODELS-01.
4. Run the gateway's health check, then return the node to the partition.
5. Note the cause in the incident ticket.

attributes.argus_summary: Steps to restore a file from the nightly or weekly backup (synthetic runbook).

body_markdown:
> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Restore a file from backup

**Service:** [Backup and Restore](/assets/nf-svc-backup) · **System:** [Backup manager BKP-MGR](/assets/nf-vm-backup)

1. Open the backup console of BKP-MGR and find the client (file server FILES-01, or the virtual machine).
2. Choose the restore point: nightly (kept 30 days) or weekly (kept 12 weeks).
3. Restore to the alternate location `\\files-01\restore\<ticket>` — never over the original.
4. Ask the requester to check the file, then move it into place.
5. Record the restore in the ticket and note the time it took.

The weekly restore test (Tuesdays) follows these steps on a sample file.

> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Service level agreement — summary

| Tier | Hours | First response | Restore target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gold | 24×7 | 30 min | 4 h |
| Silver | Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 | 2 h | next business day |
| Bronze | best effort | 1 business day | best effort |

Services and tiers are recorded on each [IT Service](/assets/nf-svc-network) record. Supplier contracts that back
them: [network support](/assets/nf-ctr-net), [storage maintenance](/assets/nf-ctr-stor),
[server support](/assets/nf-ctr-servers), [UPS maintenance](/assets/nf-ctr-ups).

attributes.argus_summary: How the facility agent on BMS-01 reads and drives the CRAC units and UPSs through serial converter SC-DH1 (synthetic).

body_markdown:
> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Data hall cooling and power control

The **facility agent** ([Facility agent](/assets/nf-proc-facility), version 3.2) runs on the virtual machine
[BMS-01](/assets/nf-vm-bms), hosted on [Hypervisor host 03](/assets/nf-hv-03). Every 10 seconds it polls the two
close-control units and the two UPSs, and it writes the CRAC setpoints.

| Unit | Protocol | Through | TCP port |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CRAC-01](/assets/nf-crac-01) | Modbus RTU, address 1 | [SC-DH1](/assets/nf-sc-dh1) serial port 1, RS-485 2-wire, 19200 8N1 | 4001 |
| [CRAC-02](/assets/nf-crac-02) | Modbus RTU, address 2 | the same RS-485 bus (terminated at CRAC-02) | 4001 |
| [UPS-01](/assets/nf-ups-01) | UPS serial protocol | SC-DH1 serial port 2, RS-232, 9600 8N1 | 4002 |
| [UPS-02](/assets/nf-ups-02) | UPS serial protocol | SC-DH1 serial port 3, RS-232, 9600 8N1 | 4003 |

## The path

BMS-01 (10.40.0.31) → management VLAN 40 → [Data hall distribution switch](/assets/nf-sw-dist-dh) port
[ge1/41](/assets/nf-sw-dist-dh-p-ge1-41) → cable DH-214 → serial converter **SC-DH1** (10.40.0.61, rack R-A01)
→ serial lines to the units.

Every element of the path is a single point of failure for all four readings: a fault on **one** unit's serial
line loses only that unit, a fault on the converter, its switch port, the VLAN or BMS-01 loses all four.

## When the agent loses the CRACs

After 10 minutes without the agent the CRACs fall back to their **local setpoint of 22 °C**: the data hall is still
cooled, but nobody sees the temperatures and the setpoints are no longer adjusted to the load. Treat a loss of
readings as urgent but not as a cooling failure; check the CRACs' own displays to be sure.

Recovery: [Serial converter SC-DH1: checks and recovery](/documents/nf-doc-sc-runbook).

attributes.argus_summary: What to check, in order, when the facility agent loses several units at once, and how to recover SC-DH1 (synthetic).

body_markdown:
> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Serial converter SC-DH1: checks and recovery

Use when the facility agent shows no data from several units at once.

1. **Is it one unit or all of them?** One unit: check that unit's serial cable and the RX/TX LEDs of its port.
   All of them: go on.
2. **From BMS-01**, `ping 10.40.0.61`. If BMS-01 reaches other VLAN 40 hosts but not SC-DH1, the fault is between
   the switch port and the converter.
3. **On the data hall distribution switch**, port **ge1/41**: link up, VLAN 40 untagged, no err-disabled state.
   After any change to the VLAN 40 port profile, check this port explicitly: the converter has no LLDP and is easy
   to miss.
4. **On the converter's console**: if it shows **192.168.127.254**, it lost its configuration (it happened after
   the power cut of June). Load the saved configuration, set 10.40.0.61/24, gateway 10.40.0.1, and **Save to
   flash**.
5. `telnet 10.40.0.61 4001` must connect. Then on BMS-01: `systemctl restart facility-agent` and watch the log for
   `poll ok` from all four units.
6. Record what you found and did on the ticket, with the root cause.

attributes.argus_summary: Moving a device off a failed switch port, and swapping in the spare switch from rack R-SP01 (synthetic).

body_markdown:
> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Replace a failed access-switch port or switch

Use when a single access point or desk loses its link while the others on the same switch work.

1. **Confirm it is the port.** On the switch: the port is down, err-disabled or shows PoE faults while the device
   end is fine. A device that comes back on another port proves it.
2. **Move to a free port.** Each access switch keeps free PoE ports (Library: **ge1/5** and **ge1/6**, VLAN 30).
   Move the patch cord, set the same VLAN and PoE profile, and update the port map in ARGUS (the cable now
   *connects to* the new port).
3. **Mark the failed port** out of service in ARGUS, with the ticket.
4. **When the switch itself must go**, take the spare from rack **R-SP01** in the Spares Store (Hub Building,
   ground floor): a **Corvane CX-48** with the current firmware. Copy the configuration from the backup, swap,
   move the cables port by port, then open an RMA with Corvane under the network support contract.
5. **Surge damage**: after a storm, check every port of the switch, not only the failed one, and note it on the
   ticket.

attributes.argus_summary: Containing, preserving evidence, assessing and notifying after an attack from outside (synthetic).

body_markdown:
> **Synthetic demo content.** Northfield IT Services, its people, suppliers and figures are fictional.


# Security incident response: an external attack

For an attack from outside: guessing logins, an exploited service, unexpected access from abroad.

## 1. In the first hour

1. **Open an incident ticket** and mark it *restricted: security incident*: only the response team reads it.
2. **Contain without destroying evidence.**
   - Block the source addresses on [Firewall 01](/assets/nf-fw-01) (the pair synchronises to Firewall 02).
   - Disable any account that logged in from an attacking address, and end its sessions on
     [VPN-01](/assets/nf-vm-vpn).
   - If that account reached a server, isolate the server in the quarantine VLAN; **do not** reboot or reinstall it.
3. **Preserve evidence** before changing anything else: export the firewall and VPN logs for the period, snapshot
   the virtual machines involved, note who did what and when on the ticket.

## 2. Assess

- What the account could reach: its groups, the VLANs the VPN profile allows (staff: VLAN 10 and 20), the
  servers it logged in to. ARGUS's **What stops if it fails?** on VPN-01 and the firewalls shows what depends on
  them if they must be taken offline.
- Which data could have been read: if personal data may be involved, tell the data protection officer **at
  once** — a breach must be notified to the supervisory authority within 72 hours.

## 3. Notify

- The head of IT and the service desk (users will notice the VPN changes).
- The national research network's CERT, with the indicators: addresses, times, accounts (synthetic contact on
  the ticket template).
- Corvane, under the network support contract, if the firewall itself is suspected.

## 4. Recover and learn

Reset the credentials, enforce MFA on every account (no exemptions), patch, restore from known-good backups if
anything was altered, and hold a review within a week. Record root cause and corrective actions on the ticket.
